instruction.text: Select the underlined word to find out which play Shakespeare is writing.

end.text: These are the opening lines of Shakespeare’s play, Macbeth. Words like “hurly-burly” might seem a bit odd, but Shakespeare actually introduced lots of language that we still use today...

instruction.text: Let’s build some of the words that Shakespeare invented.
instruction.sound: Let’s build some of the words that Shakespeare invented. Build the word alligator.

feedback.end: An alligator is a close relative of the crocodile and first appeared as a word in Romeo and Juliet.
An eyeball is the round part of the eye and first appeared as a word in Henry VI.
To gossip is to talk secretively about others. Gossip first appeared as a word in The Comedy of Errors.
A bedroom is a room with a bed where you sleep. Bedroom first appeared as a word in A Midsummer Night’s Dream.

instruction.text: Shakespeare is also famous for inventing some clever insults. Can you figure out what these phrases mean?

atoms.a: Your brain is as dry as the remainder biscuit after voyage.
The tartness of his face sours ripe grapes.
You blocks, you stones, you worse than senseless things.

instruction.text: This is another section spoken by The Witches in Shakespeare’s Macbeth. What do you notice about the lines?

atoms.a: Double, double, toil and trouble; Fire burn and cauldron bubble.

feedback.end: In lots of his work, Shakespeare enjoyed using rhyming couplets — two lines that rhyme and often have the same rhythm.

trainers.hint: The final word of the first part must rhyme with the final word of the second part.

atoms.a: The time is out of joint, O cursed spite

b.sound: That ever I was born to set it right!
I do not know how to fix it!

atoms.a: Good night, Good night! Parting is such sweet sorrow

b.sound: That I shall say goodnight till it be morrow.
I will see you in the morning.

atoms.a: I thank you for this profit, and from hence

b.sound: I’ll love no friend, since love breeds such offence.
I won’t look out for my friends if they treat me this way.
